hints: Look at the carbon skeletons first, 1-bromopropane has 3 carbons but butanoic acid has 4, so you need a step that adds one carbon.
Recall that $\text{CN}^-$ from KCN in ethanol replaces $\text{Br}$ by nucleophilic substitution to give a nitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.
Think about how a nitrile is converted into a carboxylic acid, it needs acid hydrolysis with heating to finish the job.
walkthrough:
**Count carbons to spot chain extension**

This is a chain lengthening reaction. 1-bromopropane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ (3 carbons) and butanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (4 carbons).

So reagent V must supply the extra carbon.

**Make the nitrile Q with KCN**

Cyanide ion is a great nucleophile for primary halogenoalkanes. It substitutes $\text{Br}$ and adds a carbon:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Br}^-$$
So compound Q is butanenitrile. This needs KCN in ethanol, ethanolic conditions favour substitution over hydrolysis.

**Hydrolyse the nitrile to the acid with dilute acid**

Nitriles are hydrolysed on heating with dilute aqueous acid to give carboxylic acids:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
So reagent W is $\text{HCl(aq)}$, heated under reflux. That matches KCN in ethanol followed by HCl(aq).

options.A: Correct. V = KCN in ethanol gives butanenitrile by nucleophilic substitution with addition of one carbon. W = HCl(aq) with heat hydrolyses the $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ group to $\text{COOH}$, giving butanoic acid.
options.B: Tempting because V is correct, but W is wrong. Heating a nitrile with NaOH(aq) gives the carboxylate salt, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$, not the free butanoic acid. You would need a further acidification step.
options.C: Incorrect. NH3 in ethanol converts 1-bromopropane to the amine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, with no extra carbon. HCl(aq) cannot then turn an amine into a carboxylic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. NaOH(aq) converts 1-bromopropane to propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (still 3 carbons). Oxidation with $\text{H}^+/\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ would then give propanoic acid, not butanoic acid, because no carbon was added.
